markdown:
## Team overview

- **10 builders** contribute AI-assisted work across the 30-day window.

builders.name: Ava
builders.verdictLine: Ships 45 PRs at $20 each, mostly through Devin, well below the $70 team median
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Cost per merged PR is **$20**, under a third of the **$70** team median, across **45** merged PRs.
- Devin produced **89%** of those PRs (40 of 45), and Devin compute is billed outside the gateway, so true cost per PR is higher than shown.
- Ava drives **8.7%** of team gateway spend over only **10** active days in the 30 day window.

## Why $20 per PR
- The **$900** of gateway spend is spread over 45 PRs, but only **5** of those PRs are Ava's own work.
- `claude-opus-5-5` accounts for **$486** of the spend (54%), with `gpt-6-astra` at $261 and `claude-sonnet-5` at $153.
- Prompts dominate usage: **7.56M** of 8.06M tokens are input, and completions are only about 6%.

## Good patterns
- Heavy Devin delegation produced **40** merged PRs, which keeps gateway cost per PR far below the team median.
- **0** of 420 requests failed, so no spend was lost to errors or retries.
- Context stays lean, averaging about **18,000** prompt tokens per request against a 58,000 p90.

## Bad patterns
- The costliest session was a `python` SDK script that spent **$117** on 22 requests in 23 seconds, about 4x the $26.47 median session.
- Only **24%** of prompt tokens came from cache, so most of the 7.56M input tokens were billed at full rate.
- Against Ava's own **5** PRs alone, the $900 gateway spend works out to $180 each, which shows how much the low headline cost depends on Devin.

builders.name: Ben
builders.verdictLine: Ships 20 PRs at $25 each, about a third of the $70 team median
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Yes: cost per merged PR is **$25**, roughly 36% of the **$70** team median.
- Ben merged **20** PRs over **12** active days on **$500** of spend, only **4.9%** of team spend.
- Merged work is concentrated in `proxy` (**9** PRs) and `ui` (**6** PRs), so spend maps to core product areas.

## Why $25 per PR
- **$500** across **557** requests averages about **$0.90** per request, a modest rate spread over a solid PR count.
- `claude-opus-5-5` drives the most cost at **$270**, about 54% of total spend.
- Prompts stay moderate, with a median of **25,200** tokens and a p90 of **66,500**, so context size is not inflating cost.

## Good patterns
- Only **3** of 557 requests failed (about 0.5%), so almost no spend is lost to errors.
- Cache served **3.4M** prompt tokens, about 31% of prompt volume, which cuts the cost of repeated context.
- Sessions are cheap and contained, with a median session spend of **$11.11** across **45** sessions.

## Bad patterns
- A scripted `python` SDK session cost **$65** in 22 requests, about 6x the median session, and the `sdk` scope shows **0** merged PRs to justify it.
- `claude-sonnet-5` costs about **$0.89** per request, nearly the same as `claude-opus-5-5`, so the model mix is not producing savings as currently used.
- In the 7 day sample, peak hours include **3** and **5** AM PDT, a risk sign of unattended runs that spend without review.

builders.name: Chloe
builders.verdictLine: Ships 20 PRs at $30 each, less than half the $70 team median, 15 written directly
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Cost per merged PR is **$30**, less than half the **$70** team median.
- **$600** of spend over **14** active days produced **20** merged PRs, while using only **5.8%** of team spend.
- **15** of the 20 PRs were her own and **5** came from Devin, so the gateway figure is close to her true cost per PR.

## Why $30 per PR
- **$600** spread across **694** requests works out to about **$0.86** per request.
- `claude-opus-5-5` accounts for **$324** of spend (**54%**) on 375 requests, with `gpt-6-astra` adding **$174**.
- A median prompt of **29,400** tokens keeps individual calls moderate, so most of the spend goes to frequent, short work.

## Good patterns
- **38%** of prompt tokens were served from cache, which cuts the input bill on 14.85M prompt tokens.
- Only **6** of 694 requests failed, so almost no spend was wasted on errors.
- The median session costs **$10.71** across **56** sessions, which shows short, contained bursts instead of long runaway loops.

## Bad patterns
- Her most expensive session was a `python` SDK script that spent **$78** on 22 requests in about 25 seconds, and unattended scripted traffic like this can burn money fast.
- A `claude-code` session spent **$63** in under 18 seconds, about **6x** the median session cost in a single burst.
- Her p90 prompt is **75,000** tokens, about 2.5x the median, and oversized contexts like these drive up per-request cost.

builders.name: Dev
builders.verdictLine: Ships 20 PRs at $40 each, mostly own work, well below the $70 team median
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Dev merged **20 PRs** on **$800** of gateway spend, landing at **$40 per PR** against a **$70** team median.
- **16 of 20** PRs are Dev's own work, so the low cost reflects gateway spend rather than outside Devin compute.
- Dev accounts for **7.8%** of team spend over **16 active days**, roughly **$50** per active day.

## Why $40 per PR
- `claude-opus-5-5` drives **$432** of the **$800**, about **54%**, so most of the cost is premium model usage.
- **67 sessions** at a **$11.94** median session spend means a typical PR uses about three ordinary sessions.
- About **45%** of prompt tokens (**8.6M of 19.2M**) came from cache, which keeps a prompt-heavy workload affordable.

## Good patterns
- Cache reads of **8.6M tokens** cut repeated context costs on a workload where input tokens are **94%** of the total.
- Only **9 of 831** requests failed (**1.1%**), so very little spend is wasted on retries.
- Spreading work across `gpt-6-astra` (**$232**) and `claude-sonnet-5` (**$136**) keeps some traffic off `claude-opus-5-5`.

## Bad patterns
- A scripted `python` SDK session spent **$104** in **27 seconds** across 22 requests, about **9x** the median session, and suggests a costly unattended loop.
- Short bursts are expensive: the top `opencode` session cost **$84** in **19 seconds** and the top `claude-code` session cost **$64** in **12 seconds**.
- Prompt size reaches **83,500 tokens** at p90 versus a **33,600** median, and that large context feeds the **54%** Opus share of spend.

builders.name: Elena
builders.verdictLine: Ships 10 PRs at $100 each, 43% above the $70 team median, mostly on Opus.
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Partly: **$1,000** of spend produced **10** merged PRs, which is the core of the Mixed verdict.
- Cost per PR of **$100** sits **43%** above the **$70** team median, so output is real but expensive.
- Elena accounts for **9.7%** of team spend across **18** active days, so this is steady daily use rather than a one-off spike.

## Why $100 per PR
- `claude-opus-5-5` took **$540**, or **54%** of spend, across **523** requests, so the priciest model drives most of the cost.
- Prompts are large, with a median of **37,800** tokens and a p90 of **92,000**, and prompt tokens (**24.0M**) outweigh completions (**1.59M**) about **15 to 1**.
- Each request averages about **$1.03**, so heavy context on a premium model inflates every PR.

## Good patterns
- About **52%** of prompt tokens (**12.5M**) were served from cache, which roughly halves the cost of the large contexts.
- Only **12** of **968** requests failed (**1.2%**), so little spend is wasted on errors.
- `claude-sonnet-5` handled **165** requests for **$170**, showing some routine work already goes to a cheaper model.

## Bad patterns
- A scripted `python` SDK session spent **$130** on **22** requests in under **28** seconds, about **10x** the **$12.82** median session, so automated bursts can burn budget fast.
- Short `cursor` and `codex` sessions also hit **$105** and **$80** in about **20** and **13** seconds, which suggests parallel or high-context calls that should go to cheaper models.
- Hour **0** PDT is a peak hour in the 7 day sample, so late-night runs may be getting less review per dollar spent.

builders.name: Felix
builders.verdictLine: Ships 10 PRs at $120 each, about 1.7x the $70 team median, driven by large contexts
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Felix merged **10** PRs on **$1,200** of gateway spend, which works out to **$120** per PR against a **$70** team median.
- He used AI on **20** active days across **89** sessions, so usage is steady, but output per dollar is below the team norm.
- He accounts for **11.7%** of team spend, which measures activity, not the value of what he shipped.

## Why $120 per PR
- Prompt tokens are **29.3M** of **31.2M** total tokens (about **94%**), so cost comes mainly from context sent in, not from output generated.
- Median prompt size is **42,000** tokens and p90 is **100,500**, so a typical request carries a large context.
- `claude-opus-5-5` drives **$648** of spend (**54%**) across **597** requests, so the heaviest model handles most of the work.

## Good patterns
- Only **15** of **1,105** requests failed (about **1.4%**), so very little spend is wasted on errors.
- The median session costs **$13.48**, so most day-to-day sessions stay contained.
- **7.0M** prompt tokens were served from cache, which reduces the cost of repeated context.

## Bad patterns
- Cache covers only about **24%** of prompt tokens, so roughly **22M** tokens were billed at full price despite large, repeated contexts.
- The top `python` SDK session spent **$156** across **22** requests in **29** seconds, which is scripted traffic costing over **10x** the median session.
- Short agent bursts are also expensive, with `claude-code` spending **$126** in **21.5** seconds and `opencode` spending **$96** in **14** seconds, which points to oversized context per call.

builders.name: Grace
builders.verdictLine: Spends $400 per merged PR across 5 PRs, about 5.7x the $70 team median
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Not yet on output: **$2,000** of spend produced **5** merged PRs, or **$400** each against a **$70** team median.
- Grace accounts for **19.4%** of team spend over **22** active days, about **$91** per active day.
- Spend shows heavy activity, not value, so the gap may reflect unmerged or non-PR work that this data cannot see.

## Why $400 per PR
- The denominator is small: only **5** merged PRs absorb the full **$2,000** of 30-day spend.
- `claude-opus-5-5` drives **$1,080**, or **54%** of spend, across **671** requests.
- Traffic is prompt-heavy: completions are only **6.2%** of **37.3M** tokens, with a median prompt of **46,200** tokens per request.

## Good patterns
- Requests are reliable, with **18** failures out of **1,242**, or **1.4%**, so little spend is wasted on errors.
- **31%** of prompt tokens (**10.9M**) came from cache, which lowers the cost of repeated context.
- `claude-code` carries **75%** of 7-day agent spend, a consistent primary workflow that is easy to tune.

## Bad patterns
- A scripted `python` SDK session spent **$260** in **22** requests over about **30 seconds**, a burst **13x** the **$20** median session with no visible PR tied to it.
- `codex` and `claude-code` top sessions cost **$210** and **$160** in under **23 seconds** each, so short bursts dominate cost.
- p90 prompts reach **109,000** tokens and **69%** of prompt tokens were uncached, so large context is repeatedly paid for at full price.

builders.name: Hiro
builders.verdictLine: Spends $2,500 for 5 merged PRs, $500 each, about 7x the $70 team median
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Not yet on a per-PR basis: **$500** per merged PR is about 7x the **$70** team median.
- Hiro accounts for **24.3%** of team spend but merged only **5** PRs in the 30-day window.
- Activity is steady across **24** active days and **111** sessions, so the gap is low PR conversion, not low usage.

## Why $500 per PR
- `claude-opus-5-5` drives **$1,350** (54%) of the $2,500, making it the main cost driver per PR.
- Prompts dominate tokens at **41.2M** prompt versus **2.7M** completion, a heavy context load for a small output.
- Only **5** merged PRs (4 own, 1 via Devin) absorb the full spend, which concentrates cost on each one.

## Good patterns
- Cache reads cover **15.7M** of 41.2M prompt tokens (about 38%), which cuts the cost of repeated context.
- Only **21** of 1,379 requests failed (about 1.5%), so little spend is wasted on errors.
- `claude-sonnet-5` handles **234** requests, showing some use of a lighter model alongside Opus.

## Bad patterns
- The top `python` SDK session spent **$325** on 22 requests in about 31 seconds, so scripted traffic can burn budget faster than any human review could catch.
- The top `codex` and `cursor` sessions cost **$262.50** and **$200**, roughly 9x to 14x the $22.52 median session, so a few runs inflate per-PR cost.
- Peak hours span **6** to **21** PDT, which points to long, spread-out working days with spend that is not converting into merged PRs.

builders.name: Ines
builders.verdictLine: Spent $300 across 1,516 requests with no merged PRs, against a $70 team median per PR
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Not yet: there are **0 merged PRs** in the 30-day window despite **$300** in spend.
- That **$300** would cover about **4 PRs** at the **$70** team median cost per PR.
- Usage is steady across **26** active days, but spend measures activity, not shipped value.

## Why $300 with no PRs
- `claude-opus-5-5` drove **$162** of the $300, about 54% of spend, across 819 requests.
- Input dominates output at **47.9M** prompt tokens versus **3.2M** completion tokens, roughly 15 to 1.
- The top three sessions alone cost **$94.50**, each finishing in under 33 seconds.

## Good patterns
- **45%** of prompt tokens (21.6M) were served from cache, which cuts the cost of repeated context.
- Only **24** of 1,516 requests failed (1.6%), so little spend was wasted on errors.
- Median session spend is **$2.46** across 122 sessions, so most sessions stay cheap.

## Bad patterns
- Short bursts run hot: one 22-request `claude-code` session cost **$39** in 32.6 seconds, about $1.77 per request versus a $0.20 overall average.
- Prompt size has a long tail, with a p90 of **126,000** tokens, more than double the 54,600 median, which inflates per-request cost.
- Scripted `python` SDK traffic made up **40%** of requests in the 7-day sample, with peaks at 2am and midnight PDT, so automated spend is running without producing merged PRs.

builders.name: Jonah
builders.verdictLine: Spent $500 over 28 active days with no merged PRs, so AI output is not yet shipping
builders.markdown:
## Is AI paying off?
- Not yet measurably: **$500** across **1,653** requests produced **0** merged PRs in the 30 day window.
- Usage is steady rather than idle, with activity on **28** of 30 days and **4.9%** of total team spend.
- PR scope tags list **39** entries (proxy 17, ui 14, sdk 8), but none are counted as merged, so the work may still be unshipped.

## Why $500 with no PRs
- `claude-opus-5-5` is the largest cost line at **$270** (**54%** of spend) over 893 requests.
- Three sessions alone cost **$157.50** (**31.5%** of spend) in just 51 requests, against a median session of **$3.76**.
- Prompts are large, with a median of **58,800** tokens and a p90 of **134,500**, so each request carries heavy context.

## Good patterns
- Cache reuse is solid at **52%** of prompt tokens (28.6M of 55.0M), which roughly halves the effective input cost of large contexts.
- Only **27** of 1,653 requests failed (**1.6%**), so little spend is lost to errors or retries.
- Most sessions stay cheap at a **$3.76** median across **133** sessions, showing normal interactive use is controlled.

## Bad patterns
- The top `opencode` session spent **$65** in under **34 seconds** across 22 requests, a burst pattern that burns budget fast on oversized context.
- Per request cost is about **$0.30** on every model, including `claude-sonnet-5`, so switching models alone will not cut spend without trimming context.
- In the 7 day sample, peak hours include **22:00** and **20:00** PDT, late sessions that coincide with no merged output.
